youtube.baslik: Does sliding the chair half a meter forward change the result? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In sound field testing, the patient's head should be at the point where the calibration was made. A patient sitting half a meter in front of a speaker calibrated at one meter receives, in theory, about 6 decibels more; reflections in the room may make the difference a bit smaller, but the thresholds will still be wrong. Marking the position of the chair on the floor is a simple fix.
